definition: A person who has been fully erased from official Diaspora records — no registered BCI, no tier classification, no corponation affiliation, no legal identity. Can be the result of punishment, a voluntary disappearance, or E.L.F. interference. Null addresses are theoretically invisible to the system but are also without any legal protections.
origin: Technical terminology from network architecture, adopted by underworld and civil rights communities
usage: Underworld operators, E.L.F. sympathizers, off-grid communities, Ferrogate investigators
example: Three years after the Zheng-Dao purge, Castiel became a null address by choice — no record, no safety net, but nobody could use him against his own people either.
